picks.rationale: The biggest swing on the board. Rogaratinib posted ORR 41.7% (10/24) and mPFS 31.0 mo in dSDH-GIST (PMID 42191879), the best numbers any systemic agent has put up in this subtype, and the FGF4-insulator mechanism is backed by a PDX that responded where sunitinib and regorafenib did nothing (Flavahan 2019, Flynn 2025 CT215). The catch is real: n=24 single-arm, and NCT04595747 is closed to accrual with Bayer off the program, so getting the actual drug is the hard part. If disease comes back, I want this pathway hit first.
primary_concerns: NCT04595747 is closed to accrual and Bayer has stepped back from rogaratinib, so access likely means compassionate use rather than enrollment
Single-arm n=24 with no comparator; 41.7% could shrink in a broader or less-selected population
Pan-FGFR hyperphosphatemia needs monitoring, though it tracked target engagement rather than capping the dose

picks.rationale: Same FGFR pathway, but with a door that is actually open. NCT07434843 (George/DFCI, recruiting) runs in this exact subtype, and the patient wants trials, so this is how I would cash the FGFR bet if rogaratinib stays unreachable. The PDX work hit tumors with pemigatinib too, not only rogaratinib (Flynn 2025 CT215), so the pathway logic carries across the two agents. The honest gap is no clinical readout yet, and it is another 24-patient single-arm design.
primary_concerns: No clinical efficacy data in dSDH-GIST yet; the bet rides on the rogaratinib readout plus the shared PDX response
Requires measurable disease, so it is a recurrence option, not something to start now
FGFR class hyperphosphatemia and a day 1-14 of 21 schedule to manage

picks.rationale: A durable-control play with the cleanest safety sheet in the dossier. 6/26 confirmed PR (ORR 23.1%) and mPFS 25.7 mo, with grade 3+ events in only 13.6% and zero discontinuations across the phase 1b (PMID 41184234), and it has already moved into phase 3 (NCT06640361). For a patient in their 40s who may be on therapy for years, that tolerability weighs almost as much as the response rate. Two blockers I will not paper over: the phase 3 requires SDHB-IHC loss, which this patient's stain does not currently show pending the re-cut, and the sponsor sits in China.
primary_concerns: Phase 3 entry requires SDHB-IHC loss; the patient's SDHB reads intact and needs re-stain before the dSDH label and eligibility hold
Ascentage sponsorship in China makes access a separate problem from eligibility
ORR 23.1% is roughly half the rogaratinib signal

picks.rationale: If the tumor is MGMT-methylated, this could be the highest-yield oral option on the list. The Yebra series hit 40% ORR (2/5) with 100% disease control (PMID 34426440), the patient-derived models showed on-target killing while imatinib, sunitinib and regorafenib did nothing, and about 24% of dSDH-GIST carry the MGMT methylation that predicts response (PMID 36198483). Order the MGMT test now; if it reads methylated, I would push hard for the recruiting NCT05661643 at recurrence. The honest weakness is n=5, the patient's MGMT status is unknown, and most dSDH tumors are unmethylated, so this is biomarker-gated rather than a sure thing.
primary_concerns: MGMT methylation status unknown; only ~24% of dSDH-GIST are methylated, so the predictive biomarker may not flag
Clinical signal rests on a 5-patient series
The enrolling trial NCT05661643 is in Korea, so travel feasibility is a real constraint

picks.rationale: The most direct shot at the actual driver. Belzutifan blocks HIF-2alpha, the node that succinate accumulation stabilizes in precisely this biology (Selak 2005 PMID 15652751; Bayley 2022 SDHB model PMID 35324464), and the PPGL cohort of LITESPARK-015 already showed ORR 26% with mPFS 22 mo in a sibling SDH-loss disease. Because it is approved off-label, access does not hinge on enrollment, which is rare among these options. What I cannot claim is a GIST readout: the wt-GIST cohort of NCT04924075 has not reported, so this is mechanism plus cross-indication signal and nothing firmer.
primary_concerns: No published dSDH-GIST efficacy; the case rests on mechanism and the PPGL cohort
Anemia and fatigue are expected HIF-2alpha class effects
Guadecitabine, another mechanistically-matched agent, returned 0/9 in this subtype (PMID 36302175), a reminder that target validation does not guarantee a clinical response

notes: Framing matters here. The patient is NED after R0 resection of multifocal disease plus a completely resected M1 deposit, so there is no measurable lesion to enroll on today, and every active option above is a contingency for first recurrence rather than an adjuvant order. I am deliberately not pushing chronic active therapy now: there is no adjuvant evidence in dSDH-GIST (the imatinib adjuvant RCTs structurally excluded this subtype), the tumor is indolent, and dosing a NED patient with FGFR or TKI toxicity is harm without a target. What I would do now is build the contingency stack, get the MGMT test plus the SDHB re-cut and germline SDHA resolution done so eligibility is ready, and enroll in the NCI rare-tumor registry (NCT03739827), which takes patients regardless of disease status. Recurrence is the rule in this subtype (~71%, median EFS ~2.5 yr; PMID 29413424), so the whole bet is to be ready to swing hard the moment disease returns.
